newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Good fundamentals fuel Zimbabwe shares higher.
newsitem.headline: Good fundamentals fuel Zimbabwe shares higher.

text.p: Strong economic fundamentals again propelled Zimbabwe industrial shares higher on Wednesday amid reasonable turnover.

The 57-share industrial index finished the day 198.34 points firmer at 10,204.02 -- a substantial rise after last week's consolidation and likely to continue, although not as powerfully, dealers said.

"Market and economic fundamentals are positive. The stock market had a short while to consolidate, there could be more of that later, but its enjoying putting on points again. Things are looking good," one dealer said.
Trade was fairly active and volumes were reasonable.

Meikles added 25 cents to 2,225, Delta was up 100 cents to 1,600 -- extending its surge since its two-for-one share split on Monday -- FMB put on 100 cents to 5,900, Barclays was up 175 cents to 3,400 and CAPS rose 200 cents to 1,225.
But Tanganda lost 30 cents to 390, Natfoods shed 20 cents to 630, Zimplow cut 20 cents to 650 and Border lost 50 cents to 1,150.
Trade in mining shares was quiet but stocks finished generally firmer with the seven-share index adding 53.20 points to 887.93.
Rio Tinto closed 500 cents stronger at 2,500.
